title: fix(plugin-auth): admit an MCP token minted in the same second after a password change (signed ms issue time)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X8UqWLrzTYpuat8L5eLdf2c)_
Fixes #36125
Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none
Security-touching: yes

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:改密码或重置密码后立刻用 MCP 连接的智能体和脚本,不再在同一秒内被拒绝(401),无需等一秒重试。
- 为什么做:修复「密码改了旧授权失效」规则的一个精度问题,它挡住了云端的版本对齐测试。
- 出错会怎样:若判断出错,最坏情况是改密码同一秒内的令牌被拒,和今天一样;改密码之前签发的令牌任何情况下都不会被放行。可直接撤回本改动。
- 要你做什么:无。

## What changes

The boundary, in file/function terms: `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/mcp-token-revocation.ts` `mcpConsentAdmits` refuses an MCP access token issued before its subject's password last changed. It compared `iat * 1000` (whole seconds) with the credential change time in ms by the strict less-than of `credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts` `issuedBeforeCredentialChange`, so a token minted after the change inside the same second was refused.

This takes security#2's option (a) exactly as written (comment 7064790122):

- **Source of the ms value: a claim inside the signed JWT, written by the server.** The MCP access token is a JWT the provider signs and never stores (the door refuses anything that is not a JWS compact token, so no opaque token reaches `mcpConsentAdmits`). `auth-manager-plugin-list.ts` registers an `oauthProvider({ extensions })` access-token claims contributor, `issuedAtMsAccessTokenClaim`, which writes `iat_ms` = the server clock at the mint. In `@better-auth/oauth-provider` 1.7.12 `createUserTokens` stamps `iat` first, then derives claims (`resolveAccessTokenClaims`), then signs, so the value is the mint's own instant. The client never supplies it.
- **Mint only.** The provider re-derives access-token claims at an opaque token's introspection, with `grantType: undefined`. The contributor writes nothing there, so no introspection answer carries an introspection-time value. A contributor, not `customAccessTokenClaims`, because only a contributor is handed the grant type.
- **Read only off the verified payload.** `auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts` `verifyMcpAccessTokenClaims` hands the raw claim from the same verified payload `iat` comes from; `mcpConsentAdmits` takes it as a new optional last argument.
- **Fallback refuses, never admits.** `mcpTokenIssuedAtMs(iat, claim)` uses the claim only when it is a safe integer inside the second `iat` names; otherwise `iat * 1000`, today's whole-second rule. A token minted before this release (no claim), or one with an unplaceable value, is still refused in the second of the change.
- The rule kept: `issuedBeforeCredentialChange` and its strict less-than are unchanged. The consent comparison (the consent's creation second, at most `iat`) is a separate rule and is unchanged.
- Docblocks: the one above `mcpConsentAdmits` documented the same-second refusal as deliberate; it now states the ms rule and its fallback. The MCP line in `credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts` "Where it is wired" names the ms issue time. The `/verify-email` same-second paragraph there is untouched (still true).

Accept-set change (Clause-② widening): a token minted in the second of a password change, after it, is now admitted. Every token gains one claim, `iat_ms`; no consumer's accept set narrows.

## Read first (by risk)

1. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/mcp-token-revocation.ts`: `mcpTokenIssuedAtMs` (the fallback) and the two changed lines in `mcpConsentAdmits`.
2. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts`: the `extensions` entry beside `customAccessTokenClaims` (the mint).
3. `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts`: the claim read off the verified payload.

## Two-minute verification

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/mcp-token-revocation.test.ts -t 'issue time in milliseconds'`: expect 5 passed (22 skipped). The two starred cases mint two real tokens in one frozen second (100 ms and 900 ms in) around a password change at 400 ms; both carry the same `iat`.

## Tests

New top-level `describe` in the package's existing MCP harness `src/mcp-token-revocation.test.ts` (real `AuthManager`, installed provider 1.7.12, real engine on better-sqlite3; DCR, PKCE, consent, token, refresh, `/change-password`):

- same-second token minted AFTER the change, admitted (asserts `iat` and `iat_ms` on the real token and the change time read back as second + 400 ms);
- same-second token minted BEFORE the change, refused;
- no claim (pre-fix token) in the change second, refused, with the signed claim as the control leg (admitted);
- unreadable claim (string, fractional ms, a later or earlier second, NaN, Infinity, null, object), refused each;
- the contributor writes at a mint only, never with no grant type.

<details><summary>Readings (head 8bebb598 for the suite; ablations on f2d3522c, same src blobs)</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth test` under the verify lock: `Test Files 291 passed (291)`, `Tests 6189 passed | 10 skipped (6199)`, VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck` (after building the package): VERDICT command-exit 0; `check:test-typecheck: OK`.
- Ablations, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode, anchor 1 to 0, restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty. The subject is in `src/` and the suite imports it relatively, so there is no `dist/` leg.
  - A1 claim ignored (`? issuedAt * 1000`): red on the AFTER pin, the no-claim control leg, the unit pin (3 failed).
  - A2 same-second read as after (`? issuedAt * 1000 + 999`): red on the BEFORE pin (2 failed).
  - A3 fallback admits (`: issuedAt * 1000 + 999`): red on the no-claim pin and the unreadable pin (3 failed).
  - A4 second bound deleted: red on the unreadable pin (1 failed).
  - A5 integer guard deleted: red on the unreadable pin (1 failed).
  - A6 contributor removed from the provider options: red on both starred pins and the no-claim control (3 failed).

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The ms value is the claims-callback instant, a few ms after the provider's own `iat` instant (`createUserTokens` stamps `iat`, validates resources, runs `customTokenResponseFields`, then derives claims, then signs). The grant (code or refresh token) is validated before either instant. The claim is bounded to the second `iat` names, so it can move a token only within that second. A token whose signing finishes after the change is handed to the client after the change, from a grant a password change keeps by design; a reset deletes the consent and refresh family, which the consent read refuses on its own.
- File surface: the claim named `mcp-token-revocation.ts`, `credential-change-ends-prior-access.ts`, the mint site, tests and the changeset. Reading the claim off the verified payload also needs `auth-manager-mcp-access-token.ts` (`verifyMcpAccessTokenClaims`/`verifyMcpAccessToken`): the payload exists only there. `overlap-check` on 8bebb598: clean against origin/main and 0 PR heads.
- Cloud's repro (`apps/objectos-ee/test/scim-leaver-lifecycle.e2e.test.ts`, cloud pin round 4920) is not runnable here; the platform pins above stand in. Clock skew between server instances is unchanged by this PR (security#2's clock note).
- `@objectstack/plugin-auth` changeset: `patch` with both declaration lines.

## Verification

Local scope per the dispatch: dependency closure build, plugin-auth test and typecheck under the verify lock, and the `dispatch-gates --commands` families (exit codes in the report). The repo-wide families run in CI.
